thread:
Sam: quick share — I ran a focused microbench on KV layouts vs fused flash kernels, found a surprising perf regression when switching from interleaved->separate for longer sequences. attaching numbers below. :thinking:

Jordan: can you paste the exact bench command + model shape?

Sam: sure. benchmark was small-run, 3 repeats, nvprof style. model: 30B-ish transformer, seq=2048, batch=1, kv_dtype=fp16/bf16 tests. command:
```
./bench_attention --model backbone --seq 2048 --batch 1 --kv-layout interleaved|separate --attention fused-flash|flash-paged --dtype fp16
```

Sam: raw median per-token lat (ms):
- interleaved + fused-flash + fp16: 0.95 ms/token
- separate   + fused-flash + fp16: 1.32 ms/token  <-- +39%
- interleaved + flash-paged + fp16: 1.05 ms/token
- separate   + flash-paged + fp16: 1.08 ms/token
- interleaved + fused-flash + bf16: 0.97 ms/token
- separate   + fused-flash + bf16: 1.10 ms/token  <-- +13%

Lina: whoa. so fused-flash is much more sensitive to layout. flash-paged less so.

Maya: did you control for alignment/stride? separate layout likely causes non-coalesced loads for the fused kernel path. what are strides?

Sam: good call. strides were: interleaved: stride = hidden_dim * sizeof(dtype) (packed), separate: stride = batch_stride (rounded to 256 for allocator) -> ended up 2048-byte stride for key blocks on this run.

Devon: 2048B is probably killing the L2/L1 prefetch patterns for fused kernels. flash fused does tight vector loads expecting 256/128B alignment. page-based schedules tolerate bigger strides.

Jordan: can you repro with forcing allocator to 256B stride? maybe we accidentally introduced large stride via our new cache arena.

Sam: I re-ran with forcing 256B alignment/stride for separate layout — result: separate + fused-flash + fp16 -> 1.01 ms/token (back to within 6% of interleaved). so alignment is the main factor here.

perf-bot: summary uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-perf/1769991111/kv-layout-alloc-report.txt

Maya: nice. also check dtype packing — bf16 sometimes reduces register pressure but changes memory traffic. you saw smaller delta for bf16?

Sam: yep bf16 reduced delta. hypothesis: bf16 halves memory bandwidth per element vs fp16 in our kernels because we pack/load differently (we use vectorized bf16->fp32 expand in regs).

Lina: any kernel-level asserts or bank-conflicts in the profiler?

Sam: nvprof shows a higher L1D load efficiency drop for separate+fused: 62% -> 28%. also higher DRAM read bytes up ~1.6x due to redundant loads (cache misses).

Devon: sounds like the fused kernel issues: it assumes contiguous KV per head for block-wise GEMM-ish loads. separate layout with big stride breaks that. two options: (1) change allocator to prefer small strides for KV buffers (2) adjust fused kernel to handle strided loads with a fallback (slower but correct) (3) revert to interleaved for now.

Jordan: what's the rollout risk? allocator change might affect other components. adding specialized allocation for KV buffers seems safest (a per-pool requirement).

Maya: do we have a fast memcpy fallback that can repack separate->packed on the fly and amortize cost across sequence? i.e., when stride bad, memcpy into packed staging buffer per request. That would hit latency though.

Sam: quick numbers: memcpy repack cost for seq=2048 was ~0.12 ms/token extra, which is better than 0.37 ms/token regression we saw. so repack as fallback is viable for short-term.

Lina: can we make the repack async and amortize across batch? for batch=1 it's tough. but dedicated allocator or pool with 256B alignment seems the long-term fix.

Devon: I'll prototype a KV pool that enforces 256B stride/alignment for head buffers. low-risk patch behind a flag. also add a runtime check that rejects >512B stride for fused kernel path and falls back to repack.

Jordan: also add a config knob in runtime for "kv_layout_preference": [interleaved, separate, adaptive] so teams can opt into conservative behavior.

Sam: created a tiny repro gist in our internal gists: gist.redwood/kv-stride-repro (contains the bench harness + allocator toggles).

perf-bot: flagged two perf-regressions (PR#4721) — label: perf, priority: p2

Maya: next steps checklist:
- Devon: KV pool prototype + flag (PR)
- Sam: expand bench to batch=4/8 and seq varied (512, 1024, 2048) + post results in S3
- Jordan: add runtime rejection + fallback + config knob
- Lina: add unit test that validates fused kernel path only if stride <= 512B

Sam: I'll post the S3 link after the expanded run. thanks all. :rocket:

Jordan: fyi we should also run on A100 vs H100 — H100 prefetch might behave differently. add to matrix.

Sam: noted. I'll include device matrix.

Maya: thanks — this explains a customer regression we saw on dedicated envs where their allocator uses large page slabs. good catch. :thumbsup:
